# 28. Communication Channels

This specimen tree carries the naming law alone. It states no register table, so nothing in it declares an
identifier and the declaration index reads the section as empty.

## 28.1 Naming law

**N1.** A channel's canonical identifier is a mnemonic for the conversation it carries, chosen so that no
two channels on the same boundary share a stem.

**N2.** Identifiers are mnemonic, uppercase, and hyphenated, under one of the three class prefixes the
taxonomy states.

**N5.** A link identifier and the channel identifiers it carries share no stem, so a search for one never
returns the other.

**N6.** A register is named for the store and the key rather than for a verb.
